tool_args.rationale: All five observations are positive and lie at H = 0.16–0.48, far short of the target H = 23.9. A long-horizon probe directly tests whether the response reverses sign and helps constrain the slow component before fitting.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the dual-exponential adaptation model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At short horizons, the slow term mainly constrains the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. Different values for those parameters can fit the pilot yet give different forecasts at H = 23.9.
It can explain the positive pilot response, but it cannot reverse sign. The pilot ends too early to distinguish saturation from reversal.
Finer trajectory samples do not directly test the late-time reversal that determines the target forecast.
It does not constrain the slow adaptation or test the predicted reversal.
